reasons.A: Short, plain sentences and fragments come close, but it slips into imperative how-to mode and longer explanatory sentences more than the passage's first-person narrative does.
reasons.B: Long, smoothly joined sentences, a reflective advice-giving stance and softer diction ('temptation', 'worth being patient') are far from the passage's clipped, flat voice.
reasons.C: Best matches the passage's very short declaratives, 'Then...' openings and clipped fragments in a plain first-person narrative; it is slightly heavier on fragments and opens in the present tense, but it is still the closest.
